attempts.text:
**Cost: 240 minutes, made up of 180 minutes of driving and 60 in deferral penalties.** I worked this out by hand and did not run a solver. I compared the alternatives that seemed plausible, and none beat 240, but this isn't a formal proof that it's optimal.

**Deferrals:** Bidur farm and Trishuli farm can only connect to the rest of the network through Tarkeshwar care home. Its only road out, to Suryagadhi temple, is impassable, so these 3 adults can't be reached and must be deferred (3 × 20 = 60).

**Car routes**

| Car | Trip | People rescued | Drop-off | Minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| car1 | Dhunche → Galchhi → Dhunche → Myagang | 3 Galchhi adults, 1 Dhunche adult | Myagang | 32 |
| car1 | Dhunche and back | 2 Dhunche adults | Myagang | 10 |
| car1 | Suryagadhi and back | 2 elderly | Myagang | 16 |
| car1 | Suryagadhi → Kalika and back | 4 children | Myagang | 56 |
| car2 | Gosaikunda and back | 4 children | Uttargaya | 22 |
| car2 | Gosaikunda and back | 3 children | Uttargaya | 22 |
| car2 | Shivapuri and back | 3 adults | Uttargaya | 22 |

**Alternatives checked**
- **Deferring more people:** this always costs more than it saves. The closest case is the 2 remaining Dhunche adults, where deferring costs 40 and saves only 10 minutes of driving.
- **Moving a car between evacuation points:** the Myagang–Uttargaya route takes 21 minutes each way, so a Gosaikunda trip that ends at Myagang takes 32 minutes instead of 22. It doesn't remove any other trip.
- **Combining the elderly with the Dhunche pickup:** the route Myagang → Suryagadhi → Dhunche → Myagang takes 26 minutes. This is the same as the two separate trips, so there is no saving.
